acts.desc: Host Ira Glass goes to Union Square, a 15-minute subway ride from Wall Street, where it doesn't look like we're on the edge of an economic abyss.
acts.label: Prologue
Act One
acts.desc: Alex Blumberg and Adam Davidson recount the 36-hour period, two weeks ago, when the credit markets froze. Plus, what it's like now for businesses to get short-term loans, and how the hardship is spreading to every sector of the economy.
acts.credits: By Alex Blumberg, Adam Davidson, Planet Money
acts.title: The Day The Market Died

acts.label: Act Two
acts.desc: One more confusing financial product that's bringing down the global economy. And one of way to think about this product is this: If bad mortgages got the financial system sick, this next thing you're about to hear about, helped spread the sickness into an epidemic. These are "credit default swaps." Alex explains.
acts.title: Out Of The Hedges And Into The Woods

acts.label: Act Three
acts.desc: Ira talks with Michael Greenberger, a former commodities regulator, who tells the story of when it was decided not to regulate credit default swaps. And how that decision was emblematic of the way we didn't regulate a lot of the toxic financial products we're hearing about now.
acts.title: Swap Cops

acts.label: Act Four
acts.desc: Ira and Adam answer the question: Was the $700 billion bailout bill signed into law today a good idea or a bad one?
acts.title: What's Next?
